{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.",
    "If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp drop, adjust downward by 2–5% in next forecast.",
    "After a price spike, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10% above recent peak for 3–5 days.",
    "When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model underestimates — increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.",
    "If model forecast is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows strong mean reversion, reduce forecast by 2–4% to reflect downward bias.",
    "For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently above true outcome by >5%, apply downward correction based on sentiment decay rate.",
    "If sentiment history shows multiple small positive spikes, model may overfit — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per spike.",
    "When true outcome shows volatility >10% from recent mean, model often lags — adjust forecast to match 1–2 day lagged true value."
  ]
}
